APD connects the tungsten chokepoint to semiconductor WF6 demand, but it is a large-cap reference mapping with likely low consolidated materiality unless WF6 capacity, pricing or feedstock constraints become significant.
Need primary-source verification for exact ticker formats and listing status for MEC.JP, KINSUS.TW, ATS.AT, SHINKO.JP and Guardian Metal Resources before dashboard tracking.

summary: Layer 2B maps the supplied candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships across two active chokepoint lanes: non-China tungsten/APT/WF6/carbide supply and HBM/AI-accelerator advanced-packaging substrates/chemistry. The highest-quality mapped relationships are reference anchors where the business linkage is known but segment materiality still needs verification: Sandvik via Wolfram/Buffalo Tungsten, Air Products via WF6, and Almonty via allied tungsten feedstock/oxide pathway. The more Serenity-relevant underfollowed lane is Kennametal as a downstream carbide/tooling beneficiary or margin-risk name, MEC as a copper-bonding surface-chemistry chokepoint beneath FC-BGA substrate makers, and Kinsus/AT&S/Shinko as smaller substrate makers where AI accelerator exposure may be hidden inside broader IC-substrate labels. This is a relationship map only, not a recommendation; all names require primary-source revenue exposure, customer qualification, capacity and market-pricing checks before survival into later layers.
